translationRepairs: When the You Mausoleum was being built, Qin Hui was to serve as overall supervisor but shrank from going, so Zhonghou was appointed Censor-in-Chief to go in his place.
When the You Mausoleum was being built, Qin Hui was to serve as overall supervisor but shrank from going, so Zhonghou was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs to go in his place.
Chinese 樞密使 is Commissioner of Military Affairs / Privy Councilor, not Censor-in-Chief (御史中丞/大夫).
When the You Mausoleum was being constructed, Qin Hui was supposed to serve as overall supervisor but feared going; Zhonghou was therefore appointed Censor-in-Chief in his place to go in his stead.

When the You Mausoleum was being constructed, Qin Hui was supposed to serve as overall supervisor but feared going; Zhonghou was therefore appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs in his place to go in his stead.
Chinese 樞密使 is Commissioner of Military Affairs, not Censor-in-Chief.

After coming from Yue to have audience, he told his friend Wang Qin, "Although Zhonghou and Hui are connected by marriage, Hui always harbors suspicion. I now want a memorial that will not offend the taboos of the times."

After coming from Yue to have audience, he told his friend Wang Zhi, "Although Zhonghou and Hui are connected by marriage, Hui always harbors suspicion. I now want a memorial that will not offend the taboos of the times."
Chinese 王銍 is Wang Zhi; 銍 is not Qin. Packet English wrongly uses Wang Qin.
Qin advised him only to ask to be relieved of overseeing academic affairs, but even so he was dismissed.
Zhi advised him only to ask to be relieved of overseeing academic affairs, but even so he was dismissed.
Subject 銍 continues Wang Zhi, not a person named Qin.

When the commander of the Jiankang army Bing Shun was gravely ill, the regent Lü Yiyao memorialized that Yuan replace him. The Emperor did not wish a maternal relative to command troops and did not grant it.

When the commander of the Jiankang army Bian Shun was gravely ill, the regent Lü Yihao memorialized that Yuan replace him. The Emperor did not wish a maternal relative to command troops and did not grant it.
邊順 is Bian Shun (surname Bian); 呂頤浩 is conventionally Lü Yihao.

When the Empress Dowager attended the Jingling Palace, Yuan saw her and then went out speaking slander. An edict ordered Supervising Censor Yu Yaobang to interrogate him at his home. Yuan fully confessed to false and defamatory speech and was demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Ningyuan Army and assigned to Yuanzhou.

When the Empress Dowager attended the Jingling Palace, Yuan saw her and then went out speaking slander. An edict ordered Supervising Censor Yu Yaobi to interrogate him at his home. Yuan fully confessed to false and defamatory speech and was demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Ningyuan Army and assigned to Yuanzhou.
餘堯弼 is Yu Yaobi, not Yaobang.
When Emperor Xiaozong died, Pu was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries and sent as envoy to announce mourning to the Jin state.
When Emperor Gaozong died, Pu was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries and sent as envoy to announce mourning to the Jin state.
Chinese reads 高崇崩, almost certainly 高宗崩 (Gozong d. 1187 in late Chunxi), not Xiaozong.
Xing Huan, courtesy name Wenzheng, was a native of Kaifeng.
Xing Huan, courtesy name Wenzhong, was a native of Kaifeng.
文仲 is Wenzhong, not Wenzheng.
Chen married the granddaughter of Tang Jie, who was also a granddaughter of Chao Dong on another line.
Chen married the granddaughter of Tang Jie, who was also a maternal granddaughter of Chao Jiong.
晁迥 is Chao Jiong; 外孫 is maternal grandchild.
He was promoted to Military Commissioner of Baojing Army.
He was promoted to Defense Commissioner (chengxuanshi) of Baojing Army.
承宣使 is chengxuanshi (defense/observation commissioner), not 節度使 Military Commissioner.
He was again appointed Chief Councilor, but citing illness he did not accept.
He was again appointed Chief Palace Secretary (duchengzhi), but citing illness he did not accept.
都承旨 is chief palace secretary of Military Affairs, not Chief Councilor.
He was again appointed Chief Councilor, but citing illness he did not accept.
He was again appointed Chief Palace Secretary (duchengzhi), but citing illness he did not accept.
Same 都承旨 mistranslation as idiomatic field.
When the Empress received the investiture and favors were extended, Yi was promoted to Regimental Commander of Chengzhou and Gai to Prefect of Wenzhou.
When the Empress received the investiture and favors were extended, Yi was promoted to Regimental Commander of Chengzhou and Gai to Prefect of Wen Prefecture (Wenzhou 文州).
文州 is Wen Prefecture, not 溫州 Wenzhou; avoid conflating the two.
When the Empress received the investiture and favors were extended, Yi was promoted to Regimental Commander of Chengzhou and Gai to Prefect of Wenzhou.
When the Empress received the investiture and favors were extended, Yi was promoted to Regimental Commander of Chengzhou and Gai to Prefect of Wen Prefecture.
文州 should not be rendered as Wenzhou (溫州).
Wu Yi, courtesy name Shuqian, and Gai, courtesy name Shuping, were both younger brothers of Empress Dowager Xiansheng.
Wu Yi, courtesy name Shuqian, and Gai, courtesy name Shuping, were both younger brothers of Empress Xiansheng.
Chinese is 憲聖皇后 (Empress), not yet styled Empress Dowager in this sentence.
His second daughter became Empress of Emperor Guangzong.
His middle daughter became Empress of Emperor Guangzong.
中女 means the middle daughter, not necessarily the second in a modern count.
The Jin general Liu Shifen encamped on the border of Guanghua. Dao made a surprise attack, burned his boats, and Shifen fled.
The Jin general Liu Shi'e encamped on the border of Guanghua. Dao made a surprise attack, burned his boats, and Shi'e fled.
劉士萼 is Liu Shi'e (萼), not Shifen.
Following Fei in recovering Xiangyang and other commanderies, he was appointed Protector of the Army of the Mobile Headquarters.
Following Yue Fei in recovering Xiangyang and other commanderies, he was appointed Protector of the Army of the Mobile Headquarters.
'Following Fei' is awkward; 從飛 is following Yue Fei.
His grandfather Yizhi was Military Commissioner of the Army and Navy.
His grandfather Yizhi was Military Commissioner of the Luhai Army.
陸海軍節度使 is likely the Luhai Army commission, not a generic 'Army and Navy' gloss.
Soon an edict appointed him Commissioner of the Palace Gate while also serving as Administrator of the Imperial City Bureau, and again as Deputy Chief Councilor of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

Soon an edict appointed him Commissioner of the Palace Gate while also serving as Administrator of the Imperial City Bureau, and again as Deputy Chief Palace Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
樞密副都承旨 is deputy duchengzhi/palace secretary, not Deputy Chief Councilor.

In the past, when Renzong, Yingzong, and Zhezong succeeded to the throne, some were still in infancy and some had long been raised by the empress dowager. If they were not yet versed in important military and state affairs, then for the empress dowager to hold court was fitting.

In the past, when Renzong, Yingzong, and Zhezong succeeded to the throne, some were still in infancy and some had long been raised under nurture. If important military and state affairs were not yet familiar, then for the empress dowager to hold court was fitting.
素由撫育 is nurture/upbringing, not only 'raised by the empress dowager'; 軍國重事有所未諳 is unfamiliarity with affairs.
